name: butane_tank_blowdown
title: Emptying a butane tank (blowdown, saturated-liquid outflow)
summary: Rigid tank of 0.54 l with 0.23 kg of two-phase n-butane at 25 C is emptied at 0.035 g/s for 20 min, the outflow being saturated liquid at the state of the tank. The unsteady uniform-state mass and energy balances are integrated over time (total internal energy as state variable) and the final tank and outflow states are reported.

origin.notes: Example 4.5-3 of Klein & Nellis, Thermodynamics (Cambridge University Press, 2011); EES example (c) F-Chart Software, MIT via EES-Community/ees-examples. The binary .eez companion (EES 11.912) carries the stored solution used as verification reference. Original download page in the file header: https://fchartsoftware.com/ees/examples/examples_thermodynamics_2011/chapter%204/example%204.5-3.eez

verification.summary: Compared with the EES solution stored in the .eez companion of the source file (20 variables, --ees-units): 17 agree within rtol 0.001; P and P_1 differ by 1.7e-3 (EES vs CoolProp n-butane property models, within the 0.5 % different-EOS band) and P_kPa is a kPa-vs-Pa unit-scale difference. Mass and energy balances checked at 20 min.
verification.reference: EES stored solution (20 variables) of the .eez companion ees-examples-raw/uncategorized/example_4.5-3.eez (EES 11.912), compared with tools/compare_solution.py --ees-units
verification.notes: Tool summary: '20 common variables, 3 differ (rtol=0.001); only in EES: 0; only in CoolSolve: 2'. The largest printed relative deviation, 9.99e-1, is P_kPa: the original reports it in kPa (241.296) and CoolSolve computes it in kPa too (240.88), while the tool converts the kPa reference to Pa. The largest same-unit deviation is 1.78e-3 on P_1 and 1.72e-3 on P (EES vs CoolProp n-butane models; u and T agree to 3.2e-4). The 2 'only in CoolSolve' variables are h_1 and the string Phase_1$, added by the Phase$ rewrite (README conversion log). Mass balance 0.042 kg on both sides at 20 min; energy balance dUdt = -m_dot_out*h_out = -9.0537493 W exact.
